items.headline: Nvidia reports Q3 revenue of $115.8B, up 103% year over year, and guides Q4 to about $130B
items.why: Data Center revenue of $107.6B (up 110%) and a guide above expectations show AI infrastructure demand was still accelerating going into this report.

items.headline: Semiconductor index falls 7.9% on Tuesday as Nvidia drops 5.86% a day after a 31.5% surge
items.why: A reversal this violent right after a record rally shows the AI trade is crowded and highly sensitive to valuation worries and capex concerns.

items.headline: US spot bitcoin ETFs lose $570M on a fifth straight outflow day; November outflows hit a record $4.71B and BTC slips back to about $60K
items.why: Persistent institutional redemptions are the main source of selling pressure, and a break of the $60,000 area would turn a slow bleed into a structural test.

items.headline: Fed October minutes: policy held at 3.75-4.00% on a 10-2 vote, with two members preferring a hike; officials flag rapidly growing AI-related debt
items.why: With September PCE inflation at 3.6% and the survey median expecting hikes in December and March, rate-sensitive assets are pricing a tightening cycle, not a pause.

items.headline: US-Iran talks weigh on crude as Tehran seeks sanctions relief and an end to the US naval blockade
items.why: A possible deal is the main reason oil hit a three-month low, while a reported Houthi strike on a Saudi refinery shows supply risk has not gone away.

items.headline: Reports of new US tariffs on 16 trading partners surface as markets price a 25bp Fed hike on December 8-9
items.why: New tariffs on top of a tightening Fed raise the odds of higher inflation and weaker growth together, which hurts both equities and bonds.

items.headline: Brent slips below $90 to about $89 and WTI to about $80, a three-month low, even as Goldman raises its December Brent forecast to $105
items.why: The gap between a falling spot price and a higher bank forecast shows the market is pricing a US-Iran deal now while dealers still see supply risk later.

items.headline: Gold falls 2.67% to $3,554 on Tuesday after bouncing from a $3,500-3,520 base last week
items.why: Gold is trading as a rate-expectations asset: with the 10-year yield near 4.92% and a December hike priced in, the metal has lost its safe-haven bid.

items.why: Index losses were contained by rotation into healthcare (+2.88%) and value, so this reads as a leadership change rather than broad selling.
